nodes_source.source_quote: The data used to support the results of this study are available from the corresponding author upon request.
nodes_source.description: Empirical traffic data from a freeway connecting Qingdao and Huangdao in Shandong, China, used to calibrate simulation parameters and driving behaviors.
nodes_source.reproducibility_rationale: Access is designated as upon-request from the authors, with no public link or DOI provided.

nodes_sink.source_quote: The training process, presented in Figure 8, can be finished in less than 24 hours on a computing server with NVIDIA Quadro K620 GPU
nodes_sink.description: Convergence curves showing episode reward and mean travel time during the DRL training process over 1,000,000 frames.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Empirical dataset requires email request; source code is not published. Result claims visually cohere but are unrepeatable without source code and data.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 9 presents the Q1 (25%), Q2 (50%), and Q3 (75%) of the travel times in the mainline for three scenarios.
nodes_sink.description: Temporal plot of main travel time percentiles covering 8:00 to 9:00 under no-control, PI-ALINEA, and DRL strategies.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Uses calibrated closed empirical data; evaluation protocols and parameters are stated, so logic matches conclusions, but inaccessible files block exact reproduction.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Table 2 presents mean vehicle travel times in 20 simulation experiments.
nodes_sink.description: Comparison of aggregated mean travel times across 20 varying random seed initialisations for all 3 simulated ramp scenarios.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Directly aggregates simulation results cleanly across seeds, though simulation code and baseline data files are offline.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 10 presents the temporal-spatial distribution of the mean speeds along the mainline. The results further demonstrate the efficiency of the ramp metering
nodes_sink.description: Heatmap contour charts showcasing vehicle speed patterns geographically along the track versus simulation time across the three tested methods.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Contour derivations are clear and method components specified, capped by non-public dataset and models.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 11 presents the Q1, Q2, and Q3 of the queue lengths at the on-ramp in three scenarios.
nodes_sink.description: Time-series graphs illustrating on-ramp vehicle queue interquartile intervals resulting from competing metering modes compared to unconstrained driving.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Plots effectively support observations of reduced extreme delays under DRL; blocked only by opaque backend simulation scripts.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 12 presents the mean queue lengths at the on-ramp and the red ratios (i.e., the proportion of the red phase in the simulation time) in each simulation
nodes_sink.description: Scatter comparison showing correlative trends between imposed traffic-signal red fraction and induced physical queues under the algorithmic paradigms.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Variables map directly onto derived states; high structural coherence between claimed behaviour constraint effects and simulation numbers mapped, though code missing.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 13 presents the queue lengths at the on-ramp and the occupancy downstream of the merging area for the two ramp metering methods.
nodes_sink.description: Aligned temporal trendlines evaluating real-time ramp capacity build-up versus trailing bottleneck load metrics concurrently under DRL and PI-ALINEA.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Results visually enforce text logic well; bounded up to simulation data unavailability.

nodes_sink.source_quote: The better performance of the proposed DRL method is further revealed when considering traffic flows downstream of the merge area, which is demonstrated in Figure 14.
nodes_sink.description: Staggered distribution block diagrams recording trailing total vehicle passage throughput spanning consecutive simulated operational epochs.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Straightforward downstream measurement comparison; consistent narrative coherence despite absence of reproducible source items.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 16 presents the box plot of travel time when the information of different subareas is removed, and the baseline is the result of experiments that take original data as input.
nodes_sink.description: Dispersion distributions examining time completion costs during artificially blinded zone simulations designed to prove structural algorithm dependencies.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Test systematically addresses method reliance variables as text claims. Execution instructions given, but base tool states unreleased.
